title: IT Specialist (Senior Cloud AI Engineer)

requirements.text: you must show that you have the required IT-related experience for the grade level to which your are applying
requirements.evidence: you must show that you have the required IT-related experience for the grade level to which your are applying

requirements.text: One year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service, obtained in either the private or public sector
requirements.evidence: One year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service, obtained in either the private or public sector

requirements.text: serving as a senior cloud and AI engineer, that leads the development and institutional use of technical standards and reference architectures for cloud-hosted AI solutions
requirements.evidence: serving as a senior cloud and AI engineer, that leads the development and institutional use of technical standards and reference architectures for cloud-hosted AI solutions

requirements.text: designing and implementing end-to-end AI platforms that incorporate secure data pipelines, APIs, model development and inference environments, and containerized workloads
requirements.evidence: designing and implementing end-to-end AI platforms that incorporate secure data pipelines, APIs, model development and inference environments, and containerized workloads

requirements.text: planning and executing pilots or proofs-of-concept to evaluate emerging cloud and AI technologies, and advising leadership on whether to adopt, refine, or discontinue those solutions based on mission impact, security, and implementation risk
requirements.evidence: planning and executing pilots or proofs-of-concept to evaluate emerging cloud and AI technologies, and advising leadership on whether to adopt, refine, or discontinue those solutions based on mission impact, security, and implementation risk

requirements.text: routinely explaining complex technical issues, risks, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders in ways that build consensus and secure acceptance of recommended technical approaches, priorities, and standards within a federal IT and AI policy and governance context
requirements.evidence: routinely explaining complex technical issues, risks, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders in ways that build consensus and secure acceptance of recommended technical approaches, priorities, and standards within a federal IT and AI policy and governance context

uncertain: The ten 'Required Competencies' are counted as must. The four specialized-experience items are joined by AND: all required. The 52 weeks for current federal employees is time in grade (administrative): excluded.
